summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a history of atrial fibrillation, prior stroke, dilated cardiomyopathy, diabetes, and obesity was admitted for evaluation of acute difficulty reading words, with preserved speech and comprehension. Initial concern was for TIA, but neuroimaging revealed an acute ischemic infarct in the left medial temporal lobe, consistent with his symptoms. The stroke was attributed to cardioembolic etiology, likely due to a recent period of anticoagulation interruption when he self-discontinued Pradaxa due to stomach discomfort and had a gap before restarting warfarin. His symptoms improved during the hospital stay, and he was discharged neurologically stable. He remained on warfarin, with therapeutic INR at discharge, and was instructed to follow up with his anticoagulation clinic. Other management included continued treatment for heart failure, diabetes, and foot infection from a prior admission.
